correctness.rationale: For each integer b>=2 the selected row N_k=b^k-1 has block-constant coefficient. The normalized constant-block input isometry U and sparse output isometry V give R_b=V T_q U* with q=b^(-1/2) and T_q=sqrt(1-q^2)D(I-qS)^(-1), D_kk=k^(-1/2). The inverse B has positive Jacobi square J=B*B with diag k(1+c)/(1-c), offdiag -sqrt(c k(k+1))/(1-c), c=q^2. Carleman sum of reciprocal offdiagonals diverges; the n-shifted Meixner(2,c) orthonormal recurrence yields a unitary to multiplication by m+1 on the complete discrete Meixner L2 probability space. Hence J eigenvalues 1,2,... are simple, and R_b nonzero singular sequence j^(-1/2) exactly. Zero singular multiplicity infinite; no b=1 assertion. Compactness, weak S2 and p>2 Schatten criterion follow. Independent finite Jacobi leading five inverse-square singular eigenvalues at q=1/sqrt2,1/sqrt3,0.4 agreed with 1..5 within 1.2e-13; numerical finite truncations do NOT prove the infinite equivalence.
